issues.legal_issue: An order made without the hearing required by the governing procedure may be treated as non-est and ignored, rather than as a reviewable order.
material_facts: An applicant’s challenge to a consolidation scheme was dismissed when he did not attend the hearing.
The applicant soon sought restoration and submitted an affidavit attributing his absence to illness.
The authority accepted that illness had prevented his attendance and exercised its statutory power to address his grievance.
The Supreme Court treated the applicant’s lack of an opportunity to be heard as meaning that the earlier order was not duly made under the statutory procedure.
issues.conclusion: Because the earlier order was not duly passed in accordance with the required opportunity to be heard, it could be ignored as non-est; the rule against reviewing a previous order did not prevent that result.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 42 of the East Punjab Holdings (Consolidation and Prevention of Fragmentation) Act, 1948 makes notice to interested parties and an opportunity to be heard conditions precedent to varying or reversing an order, scheme, or repartition, except where proceedings have been vitiated by unlawful consideration. Although section 42 does not confer a power of review, an order that is non-est may be ignored at any stage. Harbhajan Singh v. Karam Singh does not bar that treatment of a non-est order.

predicates.statutory_proceeding_requires_hearing: The proceeding was governed by a procedure that required an affected person to receive notice and an opportunity to be heard before the order was made.
predicates.affected_person_lacked_hearing_opportuni: The person whose interests were affected did not have an opportunity to be heard before the earlier order was made.
predicates.absence_prevented_participation: The authority accepted that illness or another circumstance beyond the person’s control prevented attendance and participation.
predicates.defective_order_may_be_ignored_as_non_es: An order made without the required hearing may be treated as non-est and ignored.

issues.definition: When a proceeding requires a hearing, an affected person lacked that opportunity, and circumstances prevented participation, the resulting defective order may be ignored as non-est.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court’s special-leave jurisdiction does not require interference where the record does not show a fit case for intervention, while unadjudicated possession-based rights remain open for assertion in proper proceedings.
material_facts: The appeal by special leave challenged a High Court judgment declining to interfere with an order concerning a consolidation scheme.
The High Court had examined the records and found no injustice warranting relief.
The High Court concluded that a report relied on by the appellant did not displace the effect of the revenue-record entries.
The Supreme Court declined to decide who was in possession, for how long, or in what capacity, and stated that any rights acquired through possession could be asserted in competent proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was dismissed because it was not a fit case for interference under Article 136; any possession-based rights the appellant might have acquired were left unaffected and could be asserted in proper proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 gives the Supreme Court power to interfere by special leave, but the Court declined to exercise it on the facts and circumstances before it. The Court did not determine possession-based rights and left their assertion to competent proceedings.

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_writ_judgment: The proceeding was an appeal by special leave challenging a judgment on a petition seeking constitutional writ or supervisory relief.
predicates.high_court_found_no_injustice: The High Court examined the record and found no injustice warranting its intervention.
predicates.supreme_court_found_no_fit_ground_for_in: The Supreme Court concluded that the case was not a fit one for its intervention.
predicates.special_leave_interference_declined_and_: The Supreme Court declines special-leave interference and leaves unadjudicated possession-based rights open for assertion in proper proceedings.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal challenges a writ judgment, the High Court found no injustice, and the Supreme Court finds no fit ground to intervene, it declines interference while leaving unadjudicated possession-based rights open for proper proceedings.
